faqs.question: What are Pharmacy courses?
faqs.answer: Pharmacy courses are not just needed for running a drugstore but also tools to join field of medical research and development as a career option. A drug/medicine before being prescribed by a doctor has to undergo tests and approvals. It is tested in a lab and studied for dosage and side effects, only then prescription guidelines are formed. Medicines then undergo clinical trials and only when after studying all possible effects of Medicine , it is introduced in market. graduates of Pharmacy courses are part of entire process and are responsible for introducing a new drug/medicine to various medical practitioners. Fundamental purpose of pursuing Pharmacy courses is to comprehend process of generating medications and pharmaceuticals for benefit and profit of humanity.

faqs.question: What is the role of the PCI in Pharmacy education?

blocks.value: Pharmacy Council of India (PCI) is statutory body which regulates Pharmacy education across country and practice of Pharmacy across country. It ensures that pharmacy courses and education are of high quality and uniform throughout country.

PCI approves institutions, prescribes course curricula, recommends standardized operational frameworks, provides guidance on professional practice of pharmacy, and adopts a system to maintain register of licensed pharmacists. Statutory recognition of professional also represents a way to confer educational and legal recognition of pharmacy professionals.

faqs.question: How do the roles of a pharmacist and a doctor differ with regard to their accountabilities?

blocks.value: Doctor checks illnesses and decides what treatment is needed but a pharmacist makes sure right medication is safely givenand also explains how to use it.
Doctors focus on overall health but pharmacists focus deeply on science of drugs.

faqs.question: Can Pharmacy students work as medical representatives or drug inspectors?

blocks.value: Yes Pharmacy graduates can work as medical representatives. They are responsible for promoting and selling pharmaceutical products to doctors and hospitals. Medical representatives are typically sought after by fresh graduates and require good communication skills and a good understanding of product.

Pharmacy graduates may also apply to be drug inspectors through government examinations. Job requires ensuring quality of drugs and their compliance with regulations or guidelines. A Pharmacy degree from an institution recognised by PCI is usually required.

blocks.value: Bachelor in Pharmacy or B Pharmacy is a course that focuses on drugs, medicines, their uses, how to maintain them, etc. It is a popular option if you want to work in the field of medical research or want to open your own medical shop. Human Anatomy, Pharmaceutics, Biochemistry, and Medicinal Chemistry are the major Pharmacy subjects that are covered in this UG course. It is a four-year course for you after completing Class 12 whereas if you have completed DPharma (Diploma in Pharmacy), you can complete this course in only three years. Pharmacy subjects include both theoretical and lab studies that are covered in 8 semesters.

career.title: Pharmacy Career Guide: Roles, Salary & Future Scope
intro: Pharmacy graduates play important roles in medication management, patient care and the development and regulation of new drugs. Students have various job options like Pharmacists, Pharmacologists, Cosmetic Scientists, Drug Inspectors, etc. The salary offered at entry-level positions is somewhere around INR 2.7 LPA , for mid-level profiles INR 3.5 LPA and for senior profiles INR 4.9 LPA .

Pharmacy freshers can either go for jobs or choose to pursue further options like an MBA in Hospital Management, Public Health courses, Clinical Research courses , etc. The top recruiters where students can kickstart their Pharmacy career are Lupin, Cipla, Piramal, Sun Pharmaceuticals, Aurobindo Pharma , etc.
